SMTO-GML-0030 — Gmail mutation outcome is unknown

GUID: 28ac7058-504a-47b4-b55f-1ce98f6aaab9
Slug: gmail-mutation-outcome-unknown
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • SMTO lost track of a Gmail change partway through. The email may already have been sent, or the draft, label change or deletion may already be done in Gmail.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Gmail in your web browser and sign in to the same account the Task used. Only Gmail itself can show whether the change went through, because SMTO lost the connection before Google confirmed it.
  2. If the Task was sending, look in the Sent folder for that email. For drafts, check Drafts; for deletions or labels, check Trash or the labels on those emails. The email may already be sent or changed even though SMTO reported an error.
  3. Only if the change is not there, ask SMTO in the conversation to do that one missing part again. Repeating a change that already happened could send the same email twice or change things a second time.

What success looks like

  • Gmail shows the email sent, or the change made, exactly once, with nothing duplicated.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened in Gmail before asking again. Then select Copy error details and send them, together with what you found in Gmail, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to resend or repeat the change until you have checked Gmail.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gmail write (send, draft, delete or label change) failed after it may already have reached Google, and SMTO could not confirm the result; for a send, the Sent-folder search by Message-ID did not find exactly one match.

What this means

  • A provider write fails after effects may have begun, and send reconciliation cannot uniquely establish the original message outcome. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • A provider write fails after effects may have begun, and send reconciliation cannot uniquely establish the original message outcome.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect original operation/message identity and authoritative mailbox state before any further mutation.

How to fix it

  • GmailService._call/_send raised GmailMutationOutcomeUnknown after a timeout, connection error, or a provider 5xx or statusless failure on a write, so treat the write as possibly applied. Inspect the live mailbox of the same account (Sent, searched with the rfc822msgid recorded for the operation; Drafts; labels; Trash) and resubmit only the work confirmed missing. Do not replay the original request.
  • Inspect live mailbox, message or thread state before repeating send, delete or another mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The original effect is reconciled and only explicitly remaining work is submitted.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
  • SMTO-GML-0036 — Google refused SMTO access to this Gmail request
  • SMTO-GML-0026 — Gmail authorization expired
  • SMTO-GML-0009 — The list of emails to change has expired
